# Transitive pure package imports in notebooks

**Goal.** A notebook can explicitly import a public pure module whose implementation depends on other checked local modules, without manually importing every dependency into notebook source. Preserve scalar-record identity, bounded replay and reliable stale-state behavior across the full dependency graph.

**Exclusive ownership.** All five `crates/cgx2-notebook-*` crates, including their examples, tests and evidence. Do not edit syntax, sema, package, CLI/compiler, emitters, runtime, verifier, effects/security/foreign, bench, root Cargo files or shared documents. Consume frozen checked-package/import metadata and scalar/record check/run APIs. The concurrent memory lane does not change those contracts.

## Dependency and visibility contract

1. Resolve the full declared-import closure of each direct notebook import from the already checked local package graph. Use the package's acyclic topology and existing listed-module/canonical-path/hash/visibility checks. Do not search unlisted files, fetch dependencies or introduce reexports/cycles. Every reached module must pass the existing pure notebook lowering/profile, including declared dependencies that happen to be unused. A private function inside its own module keeps existing behavior; a cross-module call still requires a public declaration and that source module's explicit import.
2. Keep the direct notebook import environment separate from the internal lowered-module closure. Internal inclusion must not allow `hidden.fn(...)`, `hidden.Record(...)`, qualified type annotations or full module spellings in source cells without the required direct import. Existing local/module ambiguity and reserved generated-name checks remain. A value returned through a public API may carry a transitively defined public record identity and permit its existing scalar-field projection, but naming or constructing that type in notebook source still requires its defining module's direct import. Do not erase that identity to make a value fit.
3. Lower each reached module exactly once in deterministic dependency order. Diamond graphs and multiple direct roots must neither duplicate functions/records nor silently collide on generated names. Use the same closure algorithm for executable definitions and provenance. Preserve source-order argument evaluation, checked arithmetic, existing conditional semantics and the public immutable 1–8 i64/Bool-field record profile. Transitive effectful/foreign/memory/contract-bearing or otherwise unsupported modules fail before worker execution or state publication, even when referenced only by an inactive branch or an unused declared dependency.
4. Bound graph work before recursion/large expansion: use `cgx2_package::MAX_SOURCES` (128) as the maximum unique closure modules and path depth, reject inconsistent/cyclic metadata defensively, and deduplicate shared descendants. Preserve existing notebook/function/step/depth/replay/frame limits and apply expanded-source/replay bounds to the complete deduplicated closure, before spawning a worker or appending oversized source. Do not raise existing limits to hide expansion cost. Report the actual combined function and source accounting rather than implying each module gets a separate budget.

## Provenance, state and lifecycle

5. Every importing/using cell's package provenance must include all modules in its relevant declared-import closure, plus the existing manifest and canonical-root identity. Annotation-only, record-constructor, imported/local function body and inactive-branch dependencies participate. Changing/removing a transitive module, its fields/visibility, import edges, canonical target, manifest or root must discard stale retained definitions/values and invalidate transitive notebook readers. Cells whose dependency closures do not intersect the change keep valid observations. An unrelated module outside those closures must not become a fake dependency. Package verification may conservatively block execution after any changed checked snapshot, as today; do not silently reload metadata to evade reopen requirements.
6. The parent and worker must agree on the closure and allowed canonical record identities, without treating every record in the package as visible notebook source. Preserve tagged worker size/type/field checks, nominal result checking, transactional definition/binding publication, source-span diagnostics, cancellation/timeout limits and no hidden effect replay. Failure must leave prior valid observations intact except the specifically stale dependencies.
7. Save/reopen, selected/affected rerun, Restart and Run All, clean sweep, export/import and loopback UI must handle the same closure. Package inputs remain external under the existing asset rules; do not claim exported notebooks are self-contained. Add a readable `.cgnb` with a three-level chain and a diamond package fixture, documenting direct visibility and supported/rejected cases.

## Verification and handoff

Test scalar calls and public records across at least three modules; a diamond; two roots sharing one dependency; same-named records in different modules; annotation-only/inactive dependencies; inferred transitive record results versus rejected unimported constructor/type/call access; private functions/types; missing/unlisted/cyclic metadata; Unicode and generated-name collisions; source/hash/canonical-target/root/import-edge edits; selective invalidation and independent outputs; malformed/wrong-identity worker results; cancellation/failure recovery; save/reopen/restart/sweep/export/CLI/UI. Test closure size/depth/expanded-source boundaries and dedup accounting, including failures before publication. Reuse package fixtures read-only when useful. Run all five offline notebook suites, HTTP tests, formatting and owned all-target/all-feature Clippy `-D warnings`. Commit implementation and owned evidence with exact commands/results/bounds/limitations, record knowledge, report the commit, and stop for review.
